phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra. ˹This is˺ a Book which We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺
phrases.explanation: The chapter opens with detached letters whose exact meaning early commentators entrusted to Allah while reciting them as revelation. Immediately after, the Quran is introduced as a Book sent down to the Prophet Muhammad. Calling it a revealed Book anchors his mission in divine speech rather than human invention, preparing the listener for the transformative purpose that follows in the rest of the verse.

phrases.translation: so that you may lead people out of darkness and into light, by the Will of their Lord, to the Path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy—
phrases.explanation: Commentators explain darkness as disbelief, ignorance, and error, while light represents faith and clear guidance. Although the Prophet is the one calling and teaching, the rescue happens only by the permission and grace of their Lord. That guidance leads straight to the approved religion of Allah, who is Almighty in His governance and Praiseworthy for every favor He grants His creation.

phrases.translation: Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: This phrase names the Almighty and Praiseworthy Lord of the previous verse, noting that early reciters read the divine name either as a linked description or as the start of a new declaration of praise. Because everything in the heavens and on the earth belongs solely to Him, idols that neither own nor benefit anything have no claim to human worship.

phrases.translation: And woe to the disbelievers because of a severe torment
phrases.explanation: After inviting people into light and sole devotion to the Creator, the verse warns those who reject His oneness and refuse His Messenger. Commentators explain woe here as ruin, intense grief, or a valley in Hell, awaiting those who turn away from pure monotheism because of a severe punishment prepared for persistent disbelief.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ the ones who favour the life of this world over the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers threatened in the previous verse are defined by their priorities. They choose fleeting worldly pleasures and disobedience over obedience to Allah and the lasting reward of the Hereafter. By treating immediate appetite and status as more valuable than eternal accountability, they invert the true worth of both worlds and trade away their own salvation.

phrases.translation: and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked. It is they who have gone far astray
phrases.explanation: Not content with turning away themselves, they actively block others who wish to believe and follow the Messenger. Commentators explain that seeking to make Allah's path crooked means trying to distort His upright religion through falsehood, slander, and fabricated doubts. People who both abandon truth and sabotage it for others have wandered far from guidance.

phrases.translation: We have not sent a messenger except in the language of his people to clarify ˹the message˺ for them.
phrases.explanation: Every community before the Prophet Muhammad that received a messenger was addressed in its own tongue and dialect so that Allah's commands and prohibitions would be unmistakable. Delivering revelation in the language people actually speak removes any excuse of incomprehension and establishes clear proof before judgment.

phrases.translation: Then Allah leaves whoever He wills to stray and guides whoever He wills. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Once the messenger has made the message plain, the outcome of hearts rests with Allah, who forsakes whom He wills and grants success to whom He wills. Commentators note that none can resist the Almighty in what He decrees, and He remains All-Wise in how He guides, tests, and judges His creatures.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs, ˹ordering him,˺ “Lead your people out of darkness and into light,
phrases.explanation: Moses is presented as an earlier example matching the mission of Muhammad. Commentators explain the signs given to Moses either as clear proofs in general or specifically as the nine miraculous signs shown in Egypt, all aimed at calling his people out of error and disbelief into the light of faith.

phrases.translation: and remind them of Allah’s days ˹of favour˺.” Surely in this are signs for whoever is steadfast, grateful
phrases.explanation: Most early commentators explained Allah's days as His memorable favors upon the Israelites, such as rescuing them from Pharaoh, parting the sea, shading them with clouds, and sending manna and quails, while another view included past days of judgment on rebellious nations. Remembering those turning points offers lasting lessons for every servant who is patient in trial and grateful in blessing.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ when Moses said to his people, “Remember Allah’s favour upon you when He rescued you from the people of Pharaoh,
phrases.explanation: Fulfilling his command to remind them, Moses calls the Children of Israel to recall Allah's great deliverance from Pharaoh's regime and followers. True gratitude begins with concrete memory, looking back honestly at the days of helplessness when only divine intervention could break a tyrant's grip and bring freedom.

phrases.translation: who afflicted you with dreadful torment—slaughtering your sons and keeping your women. That was a severe test from your Lord
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh's people subjected them to relentless humiliation alongside slaughtering their newborn boys and sparing their girls for servitude. Commentators note that the Arabic word translated as test can mean either a severe trial in the suffering they endured or a tremendous blessing in the rescue that followed, since both hardship and deliverance test human faith.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when your Lord proclaimed, ‘If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more.
phrases.explanation: Moses reminds his people of a solemn divine proclamation made known to them after their rescue. If they respond to deliverance with gratitude through obedience to Allah's commands, He promises to increase His favors upon them, while some early commentators added that He also increases their capacity for obedience and further gratitude.

phrases.translation: But if you are ungrateful, surely My punishment is severe.’”
phrases.explanation: The other half of the proclamation warns that ingratitude is never a harmless oversight. Denying Allah's blessings by disobeying His commands, violating His limits, and turning away from thankfulness exposes a community to severe punishment, just as earlier ungrateful nations were seized when they rejected their Lord's favors.

phrases.translation: Moses added, “If you along with everyone on earth were to be ungrateful, then ˹know that˺ Allah is indeed Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.”
phrases.explanation: Moses makes clear that the command to be grateful is entirely for human benefit, not because God needs human tribute. Even if the Israelites and every inhabitant of the earth disbelieved at once, Allah would remain completely free of need of His creation and intrinsically Praiseworthy for His countless favors.

phrases.translation: Have you not ˹already˺ received the stories of those who were before you: the people of Noah, ’Âd, Thamûd, and those after them? Only Allah knows how many they were.
phrases.explanation: The warning widens to the vanished communities of Noah, Ad, Thamud, and countless generations after them whose true numbers and genealogies only Allah knows. Early commentators cited this clause to caution against claiming exhaustive knowledge of ancient lineages, stressing how vast the history of tested nations truly is.

phrases.translation: Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands over their mouths
phrases.explanation: When messengers brought unmistakable miracles and proofs, those nations reacted with hostility captured in a vivid gesture. Early commentators offered several explanations: biting their own fingertips in rage against the messengers, placing their hands over the messengers' mouths to silence them, gesturing in amazed denial, or refusing to speak the truth.

phrases.translation: and said, “We totally reject what you have been sent with, and we are certainly in alarming doubt about what you are inviting us to.”
phrases.explanation: Whatever physical gesture accompanied their refusal, their spoken answer to the prophets was open rejection. They declared flat disbelief in the message of divine oneness and claimed to be in unsettling, suspicious doubt about the call to abandon their idols for the exclusive worship of Allah.

phrases.translation: Their messengers asked ˹them˺, “Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?
phrases.explanation: The messengers answer their people's claim of doubt with amazement: how can anyone harbor doubt about Allah when He is the Originator who brought the heavens and the earth into existence without precedent? The entire cosmos testifies that its Creator alone deserves worship without partner.

phrases.translation: He is inviting you in order to forgive your sins, and delay your end until your appointed term.”
phrases.explanation: Far from seeking anything from them, Allah calls them to faith and obedience so that He may pardon their past sins and let them live out their full appointed lifespan in peace, rather than cutting them off early through a punishment of destruction in this world.

phrases.translation: They argued, “You are no more than humans like us! You ˹only˺ wish to turn us away from what our forefathers worshipped. So bring us some compelling proof.”
phrases.explanation: The disbelieving nations object that the messengers are ordinary human beings rather than angels, accusing them of merely wanting to sever the community from ancestral idol worship. Ignoring the proofs already shown, they demand some unmistakable authority on their own terms to prove the messengers' truthfulness.

phrases.translation: Their messengers said to them, “We are ˹indeed˺ only humans like you, but Allah favours whoever He chooses of His servants.
phrases.explanation: The messengers readily agree that they are human beings from the children of Adam, sharing the same outward form as their audience. Being human does not disqualify prophethood, because Allah bestows His grace and revelation upon whichever of His servants He chooses to guide and entrust with His message.

phrases.translation: It is not for us to bring you any proof without Allah’s permission. And in Allah let the believers put their trust
phrases.explanation: Miracles and decisive proofs are not tools that prophets manufacture at will to satisfy a skeptical crowd. A messenger can bring a sign only when Allah commands and permits it, so true believers place their reliance and confidence entirely in Allah rather than in human bargaining.

phrases.translation: Why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has truly guided us to ˹the very best of˺ ways?
phrases.explanation: The messengers explain why their reliance on Allah is unshakable: He has already shown them the clear path of truth and deliverance from His punishment. Someone who has been blessed with divine guidance has every reason to trust Allah's protection and care when facing hostility from people who reject Him.

phrases.translation: Indeed, we will patiently endure whatever harm you may cause us. And in Allah let the faithful put their trust.”
phrases.explanation: Instead of retaliating or compromising their call, the messengers pledge to bear every insult and persecution patiently for Allah's sake as they summon their people away from idols. They close by repeating that all who truly rely on anyone must place their trust in Allah alone.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers then threatened their messengers, “We will certainly expel you from our land, unless you return to our faith.”
phrases.explanation: When argument failed, the disbelievers turned to coercion, threatening to banish the messengers from their towns unless they came back into the communal religion of idol worship. Commentators note that saying return means joining their creed, even though the prophets themselves had never been idolaters.

phrases.translation: So their Lord revealed to them, “We will surely destroy the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: At the height of the threat against His messengers, Allah comforted them with a decisive revelation. Those who wronged themselves by placing worship in idols instead of their Creator and persecuting the prophets would certainly be destroyed, proving that worldly intimidation cannot outlast divine decree.

phrases.translation: and make you reside in the land after them. This is for whoever is in awe of standing before Me and fears My warning.”
phrases.explanation: Allah promised the messengers and believers that they would inherit the land after their oppressors perished, a pattern that also consoled the Prophet Muhammad against the threats of Quraysh. This promise of triumph in this world and reward in the next belongs to everyone who fears standing before Allah for reckoning and heeds His warning.

phrases.translation: And both sides called for judgment, so every stubborn tyrant was doomed
phrases.explanation: Commentators explain that the messengers prayed to Allah for victory and judgment against their oppressors, while another view adds that the disbelievers themselves recklessly dared punishment to fall. When Allah's verdict came, every arrogant tyrant who stubbornly opposed the truth and refused to worship Allah alone was brought to ruin.

phrases.translation: Awaiting them is Hell, and they will be left to drink oozing pus
phrases.explanation: Worldly destruction is not the end of the tyrant's fate, because ahead of every arrogant rejecter lies Hell. Commentators explain that the only drink offered there for burning thirst is foul liquid oozing from the flesh, skin, and interiors of the damned, mixed with pus and blood.

phrases.translation: which they will sip with difficulty, and can hardly swallow.
phrases.explanation: Driven by extreme thirst, the sufferer tries to gulp the scalding, repulsive drink little by little, yet intense loathing and burning heat make it almost impossible to swallow down. Reported prophetic traditions explain that when the liquid is finally forced down, it tears through the insides.

phrases.translation: Death will overwhelm them from every side, yet they will not ˹be able to˺ die. Awaiting them still is harsher torment
phrases.explanation: Causes of death press in from every direction and through every limb, leaving the soul trapped at the throat without either departing to grant the rest of death or settling back to allow any comfort in life. Beyond even that agony, a still harsher and unrelenting punishment lies ahead.

phrases.translation: The parable of the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that of ashes fiercely blown away by wind on a stormy day.
phrases.explanation: To show the fate of works done without faith in Allah, the verse compares the deeds of disbelievers to fine ashes caught by a violent wind on a tempestuous day. Just as storm winds scatter ash until nothing can be gathered back, disbelief strips away any lasting value from their worldly efforts.

phrases.translation: They will gain nothing from what they have earned. That is ˹truly˺ the farthest one can stray
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection they will find no benefit or protection from the deeds they counted on in life, because those works were not performed purely for Allah. Investing an entire lifetime in actions that vanish when needed most is the furthest possible straying from the right path.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth for a reason?
phrases.explanation: The listener is invited to reflect with the eye of the heart on the creation of the heavens and the earth in truth and justice by Allah alone, without partner or helper. A universe built with purpose and power testifies that its Maker governs human accountability with equal seriousness.

phrases.translation: If He wills, He can eliminate you and produce a new creation
phrases.explanation: The One who originated the heavens and the earth out of nothing is never dependent on stubborn humanity. If He wills, He can destroy and remove those who disobey Him and bring forth an entirely new creation in their place who are obedient to His command.

phrases.translation: And that is not difficult for Allah ˹at all˺
phrases.explanation: Sweeping away a rebellious people and bringing an entirely new creation into existence in their place poses no hardship, effort, or obstacle for Allah. Because His power is complete over everything He wills to do, human defiance harms only the defiant and never weakens the Lord of creation.

phrases.translation: They will all appear before Allah, and the lowly ˹followers˺ will appeal to the arrogant ˹leaders˺, “We were your ˹dedicated˺ followers, so will you ˹then˺ protect us from Allah’s torment in any way?”
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection all creation will come forth from their graves onto an open plain before Allah, with nothing hidden. There the weak followers who obeyed corrupt leaders in idol worship and rejection of the prophets will ask those proud chiefs whether they can now deflect even a fraction of Allah's punishment.

phrases.translation: They will reply, “Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. ˹Now˺ it is all the same for us whether we suffer patiently or impatiently, there is no escape for us.”
phrases.explanation: Stripped of worldly prestige, the leaders confess their own bankruptcy: had they possessed any guidance or way to avert punishment, they would have used it. Commentators recount traditions that the people of the Fire will try both weeping and long endurance, only to admit that panic and patience are alike when no escape remains.

phrases.translation: And Satan will say ˹to his followers˺ after the judgment has been passed, “Indeed, Allah has made you a true promise. I too made you a promise, but I failed you.
phrases.explanation: Once judgment is sealed and the people of Paradise and the Fire have entered their abodes, Satan will stand to address those who followed him. He confesses that Allah's promise of resurrection, reward, and punishment was completely true, whereas his own promises of safety and triumph were lies that he now betrays.

phrases.translation: I did not have any authority over you. I only called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves.
phrases.explanation: Satan strips away their excuse by reminding them that he held no compelling power or proof to force them into sin. He merely invited them to disobey Allah and follow desire, and they eagerly answered of their own choice, meaning all blame rests squarely on their own souls.

phrases.translation: I cannot save you, nor can you save me. Indeed, I denounce your previous association of me with Allah ˹in loyalty˺. Surely the wrongdoers will suffer a painful punishment.”
phrases.explanation: Neither the tempter nor the tempted can rescue the other from torment. Satan openly disowns their having made him a partner alongside Allah through obeying him in the world, and the scene closes with the verdict that wrongdoers who reject Allah face a painful punishment.

phrases.translation: Those who believe and do good will be admitted into Gardens, under which rivers flow—to stay there forever by the Will of their Lord—where they will be greeted with “Peace!”
phrases.explanation: In direct contrast to the followers of Satan and arrogant leaders, those who affirm Allah's oneness, trust His messengers, and perform righteous deeds enter Gardens with rivers flowing beneath them. By their Lord's command and grace they dwell there forever, welcomed by the angels with greetings of peace and security.

phrases.translation: Do you not see how Allah compares a good word to a good tree? Its root is firm and its branches reach the sky
phrases.explanation: Allah sets forth a vivid parable comparing a good word to a noble, fruitful tree. Early commentators explained the good word as the testimony of faith that there is no god but Allah, or the believer himself, and identified the good tree with the date palm, whose root is anchored deep in the believer's heart while his righteous deeds rise to heaven.

phrases.translation: ˹always˺ yielding its fruit in every season by the Will of its Lord.
phrases.explanation: Just as a blessed tree produces nourishment in its appointed times by its Lord's leave, firmly rooted faith continually yields righteous words and deeds. Commentators variously explained every season as morning and evening, every hour of night and day, or every recurring harvest season, as the believer's good works ascend to Allah.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah sets forth parables for the people, so perhaps they will be mindful
phrases.explanation: By clothing spiritual realities in familiar images from nature, Allah makes the difference between living faith and barren disbelief clear to human understanding. These parables are given so that people will reflect on Allah's proof, remember their duty, and turn away from error toward obedience.

phrases.translation: And the parable of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted from the earth, having no stability
phrases.explanation: In contrast, the evil word of disbelief and idol worship, or the disbeliever himself, is compared to a foul plant such as the bitter colocynth gourd. Uprooted from the surface of the soil, it has no firm root on earth and no branches rising upward, symbolizing deeds that gain neither stability here nor acceptance with Allah.

phrases.translation: Allah makes the believers steadfast with the firm Word ˹of faith˺ in this worldly life and the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: Allah strengthens believers through the firm testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger. Commentators cite prophetic traditions explaining that this steadfastness protects believers during the trials of life, when questioned by the angels in the grave, and at the reckoning of the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: And Allah leaves the wrongdoers to stray. For Allah does what He wills
phrases.explanation: Those who wrong themselves through disbelief and hypocrisy are left without that firm anchor, faltering in worldly trials and when questioned by the angels in their graves. Allah alone grants steadfastness to the faithful or leaves the unjust to stray according to His sovereign will and wisdom.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen those ˹disbelievers˺ who meet Allah’s favours with ingratitude and lead their own people to their doom
phrases.explanation: Early commentators explained this verse historically regarding the polytheist leaders of Quraysh, especially those who fought at Badr. Allah blessed them with the Sanctuary of Mecca and sent the Prophet Muhammad from among their own kin, yet they exchanged that supreme favor for disbelief and led their followers into ruin.

phrases.translation: In Hell they will burn. What an evil place for settlement
phrases.explanation: This verse clarifies the ultimate house of ruin into which those leaders led their followers after their worldly defeat. Beyond the battlefield, their final destination is Hell, where they are scorched by its flames in a wretched place of settlement for anyone who enters it.

phrases.translation: They set up equals to Allah to mislead ˹others˺ from His Way.
phrases.explanation: Those who exchanged divine blessing for ingratitude set up idols and rivals as partners alongside Allah. Commentators note two established readings of the verb, meaning either that they set up rivals to mislead others from Allah's path or that they themselves stray far from His way.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Enjoy yourselves! Surely your destination is the Fire.”
phrases.explanation: The command to enjoy themselves for a little while in this world is not permission to sin, but a stern warning and rebuke. Any brief worldly pleasure gained through rebellion against Allah quickly vanishes, and their inevitable journey ends in the punishment of the Fire.

phrases.translation: Tell My believing servants to establish prayer and donate from what We have provided for them—openly and secretly—
phrases.explanation: Turning from the ungrateful to the faithful, Allah instructs the Prophet to command believers to show true gratitude in action. They are to establish the five obligatory prayers with their proper conditions and spend in charity from the provision Allah has granted them, both privately and publicly.

phrases.translation: before the arrival of a Day in which there will be no ransom or friendly connections
phrases.explanation: Believers must fulfill these duties now before the Day of Resurrection arrives, when no bargaining or ransom will be accepted to buy a guilty soul out of punishment. On that Day no worldly friendship will intercede to set aside divine justice, leaving only relationships built for Allah's sake.

phrases.translation: It is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and sends down rain from the sky, causing fruits to grow as a provision for you.
phrases.explanation: The passage grounds exclusive worship in unmistakable blessings that everyone can witness around them. Allah alone created the heavens and the earth from nothing and sends down rain from the clouds to revive trees and crops, producing varied fruits as nourishment and sustenance for human life.

phrases.translation: He has subjected the ships for your service, sailing through the sea by His command, and has subjected the rivers for you
phrases.explanation: He also made ships serviceable so people can ride across the seas and transport goods from town to town by His command, and He placed fresh rivers across the earth for drinking and cultivation. Lifeless idols have no share in creating or governing any of these gifts.

phrases.translation: He has ˹also˺ subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constantly orbiting, and has subjected the day and night for you
phrases.explanation: Above the earth, Allah placed the sun and the moon in unceasing motion to serve human life, seasons, and reckoning, while commentators add that both bodies remain tirelessly obedient to Allah's command. Day and night likewise alternate in mercy so people can seek their livelihood by light and rest in darkness.

phrases.translation: And He has granted you all that you asked Him for.
phrases.explanation: Alongside cosmic provisions, Allah grants people a share of everything they ask of Him and need for survival. Commentators also note a reading and interpretation meaning that He gives them both what they ask for and countless vital blessings, like sun, moon, day, and night, that they never even thought to request.

phrases.translation: If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you would never be able to number them. Indeed humankind is truly unfair, ˹totally˺ ungrateful
phrases.explanation: If human beings attempted to tally Allah's favors, they could never count their number, let alone repay them in full without His help. Yet the disbelieving human being remains deeply unjust and ungrateful whenever he enjoys the Creator's gifts while directing thanks and worship to false gods.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Abraham prayed, “My Lord! Make this city ˹of Mecca˺ secure, and keep me and my children away from the worship of idols
phrases.explanation: Against the backdrop of Meccan idol worship, the chapter recalls Abraham praying for the Sanctuary of Mecca to be a city of safety for its inhabitants. Despite his rank as Allah's intimate friend, he humbly begged Allah to keep him and his children far away from worshipping carved idols, reminding every believer that no one should feel immune to trial.

phrases.translation: My Lord! They have caused many people to go astray.
phrases.explanation: Abraham explains his dread of idols by pointing to the trail of ruin they leave behind in human history. Though carved stones cannot speak or act on their own, attachment to them has caused multitudes of people to veer away from the straight path and reject their Creator.

phrases.translation: So whoever follows me is with me, and whoever disobeys me—then surely You are ˹still˺ All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Whoever follows Abraham's way of pure monotheism and obedience belongs to his community and path. As for someone who disobeys, Abraham does not curse him, entrusting his case to Allah as All-Forgiving and Most Merciful toward whoever repents, a prayer that moved the Prophet Muhammad to weep in compassion for his own community.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! I have settled some of my offspring in a barren valley, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer.
phrases.explanation: Commentators recount how Abraham brought Ishmael and his mother Hagar to the crop-free valley of Mecca beside the site of the Sacred House in obedience to Allah's command. Turning back at the mountain pass, he prayed that this settlement in a barren land would be dedicated to establishing prayer for Allah alone.

phrases.translation: So make the hearts of ˹believing˺ people incline towards them and provide them with fruits, so perhaps they will be thankful
phrases.explanation: Abraham asked Allah to draw the hearts of believers in yearning toward his family and to supply that uncultivated valley with fruits and sustenance. Allah answered his prayer through the gushing of Zamzam, the settlement of Mecca, and the pilgrimage of nations, so that its inhabitants would respond with gratitude.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! You certainly know what we conceal and what we reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah
phrases.explanation: Abraham calls upon Allah as witness to the sincerity of his prayers and his concern for his family. Allah knows every unspoken intention hidden in the heart as well as every word uttered aloud, since nothing in the earth or the heavens can be concealed from the One who created and governs them all.

phrases.translation: All praise is for Allah who has blessed me with Ishmael and Isaac in my old age. My Lord is indeed the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers
phrases.explanation: Practicing the very gratitude he asked for his descendants, Abraham praises Allah for granting him his sons Ishmael and Isaac after he had reached advanced old age. That miraculous gift confirmed from personal experience that his Lord hears and answers every sincere supplication raised to Him.

phrases.translation: My Lord! Make me and those ˹believers˺ of my descendants keep up prayer. Our Lord! Accept my prayers
phrases.explanation: Even after decades of faithful devotion, Abraham asks Allah to keep him steadfast in fulfilling the obligation of prayer and to raise prayer-observant believers from among his offspring. He concludes by begging his Lord to accept both his supplication and his wider acts of worship.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the judgment will come to pass.”
phrases.explanation: Abraham closes his prayer by seeking forgiveness for himself, his parents, and all believers who follow the path of faith on the Day when people stand for the Reckoning. Commentators note that his prayer for his father was made because of an earlier promise, before it became clear to Abraham that his father would die an enemy of Allah.

phrases.translation: Do not think ˹O Prophet˺ that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.
phrases.explanation: Addressing the Prophet directly, Allah assures him that He is never heedless of the crimes and rejection committed by the wrongdoers. As early commentators observed, this declaration serves simultaneously as a stern warning to oppressors and a deep consolation to the wronged, because every deed is recorded.

phrases.translation: He only delays them until a Day when ˹their˺ eyes will stare in horror—
phrases.explanation: Worldly respite must never be mistaken for divine approval or forgetfulness of human injustice. Allah merely defers the punishment of the wrongdoers until an appointed Day of Judgment, when the sudden terror of what they behold will freeze the gazes of creation in a stiff, unblinking stare.

phrases.translation: rushing forth, heads raised, never blinking, hearts void
phrases.explanation: Summoned from their graves, they hasten forward toward the caller with their heads lifted up and their eyes locked open without blinking. Commentators explain that their hearts are void because terror has driven them to their throats and left their minds utterly hollow, unable to grasp or retain any good.

phrases.translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will overtake ˹the wicked among˺ them, and the wrongdoers will cry, “Our Lord! Delay us for a little while. We will respond to Your call and follow the messengers!”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to warn people now of the Day when torment will seize the wrongdoers and they will beg for a brief return to worldly life so they can answer Allah's call and obey the messengers. Their plea comes only after the time for testing has ended.

phrases.translation: ˹It will be said,˺ “Did you not swear before that you would never be removed ˹to the next life˺?”
phrases.explanation: Their desperate request for more time is met with a stinging rebuke recalling their solemn oaths in the world. They had sworn earnestly that they would never pass from this life into resurrection and judgment, or that their worldly power and station would never end.

phrases.translation: You passed by the ruins of those ˹destroyed peoples˺ who had wronged themselves. It was made clear to you how We dealt with them, and We gave you ˹many˺ examples
phrases.explanation: The rebuke continues by reminding them that they lived in and traveled through the lands of destroyed nations like Noah's people, Ad, and Thamud. They saw clearly how Allah punished persistent defiance, and they heard the parables and warnings sent through revelation, yet they refused to repent while time remained.

phrases.translation: They devised every plot, which was fully known to Allah, but their plotting was not enough to ˹even˺ overpower mountains ˹let alone Allah˺
phrases.explanation: Those rebellious peoples devised schemes of idolatry, falsehood, and opposition to the prophets, all of which Allah fully encompassed in knowledge. Commentators note two readings and explanations of the final clause: that their scheming was far too weak to move mountains or shake Allah's religion, or, in another reading linked to tales of an ancient tyrant, that their plots were so audacious they nearly shook the mountains, yet still harmed only themselves.

phrases.translation: So do not think ˹O Prophet˺ that Allah will fail to keep His promise to His messengers. Allah is indeed Almighty, capable of punishment
phrases.explanation: Strengthening the Prophet's heart, Allah affirms that He will never break His promise to give His messengers victory and judge those who belie them, just as He fulfilled it for earlier prophets. None can escape the Almighty when He wills to take retribution against persistent rejecters.

phrases.translation: ˹Watch for˺ the Day ˹when˺ the earth will be changed into a different earth and the heavens as well, and all will appear before Allah—the One, the Supreme
phrases.explanation: Divine retribution will be completed on the Day when this earth and the heavens are replaced by another earth and heavens. Commentators record traditions describing the new earth as pure white like silver, unstained by bloodshed or sin, while people cross the bridge over Hell and come forth from their graves completely exposed before Allah, the One, the irresistible Subduer.

phrases.translation: On that Day you will see the wicked bound together in chains
phrases.explanation: On that Day of cosmic transformation, the guilty who associated partners with Allah and rejected His messengers will behold one another yoked together in chains. Commentators explain that their hands and feet will be bound to their necks in iron collars and fetters in shared humiliation.

phrases.translation: with garments of tar, and their faces covered with flames
phrases.explanation: They are clothed in shirts of pitch-black tar like that smeared on camels, which ignites rapidly and clings to the skin, while another early reading describes garments of molten copper heated to its utmost intensity. Meanwhile, fire envelops and scorches their faces from every side.

phrases.translation: As such, Allah will reward every soul for what it has committed. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation: All of this unfolds so that Allah may justly recompense every soul for the good or evil it earned in life. Allah is swift in reckoning because His knowledge already encompasses every deed, great or small, needing no effort or delay to calculate the exact account of all creation.

phrases.translation: This ˹Quran˺ is a ˹sufficient˺ message for humanity so that they may take it as a warning and know that there is only One God, and so that people of reason may be mindful
phrases.explanation: Ending where it began, the chapter declares the Quran a complete proclamation for humanity. Through its warnings and signs in creation and history, people are called to guard against Allah's wrath, know with certainty that He is the only One God worthy of worship, and let sound minds take lasting admonition.
